blockingFindings.summary: Endpoint absence is resolved by gold/local identifier equality rather than entity identity.
blockingFindings.evidence: _endpoint_resolution looks up predicted_entities.get(goldEntityId). In an adversarial review case, gold endpoints g1/g2 and predicted candidates c17/c42 had identical type/span signatures; relation semantic TP was 1, but endpointResolution.missing was 2 and missingEndpointRate was 1.0.
blockingFindings.impact: Correct predicted entities receive a 100% missing-endpoint rate whenever local candidate IDs differ from gold IDs, which local stage-1 IDs are allowed to do. The approved endpoint threshold is therefore not execution-safe.
blockingFindings.requiredRemediation: Resolve each gold endpoint against the immutable candidate table by the registered typed-span identity or an explicit server-owned gold-to-candidate mapping, enforce one-to-one matching, and test arbitrary local-ID renaming, duplicate semantic candidates, absent candidates, drift and wrong type.

blockingFindings.summary: Trigger occurrence metadata is not materialized strongly enough to prove the quoted trigger.
blockingFindings.evidence: _trigger_supported checks digest, containment and occurrence count but never binds occurrence width/content to triggerQuote. An adversarial review case supplied triggerQuote='supports' with occurrence span [10,11]; it still received evidence exact=1 although the quote is eight code points long.
blockingFindings.impact: Malformed or incorrectly materialized occurrence metadata can pass the evidence hard gate and inflate exact/support rates despite not identifying the quoted predicate trigger.
blockingFindings.requiredRemediation: Use a server-owned occurrence record bound to quote digest and validated source slice, require half-open span width/content to match triggerQuote under the registered Unicode policy, validate sentence/clause/source bounds, and add width mismatch, content mismatch, repeated occurrence and Unicode adversarial tests.

constraints: Preserve all v1-v3 packages and review artifacts as immutable history.
Do not preregister, freeze an execution package, authorize provider execution or inspect held-out data from RM-20C.
A superseding offline package requires a separate owner re-review.
